'''Wan Huilin''' ({{zh|s=万惠霖}}; 20 November 1938 – 28 April 2024) was a Chinese physical chemist who was a professor at [[Xiamen University]], and an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. He was a member of the [[Chinese Communist Party]] (CCP).<ref name="ra"/> 

== Biography ==
Wan was born in [[Hankou]], [[Hubei]], on 20 November 1938.<ref name="ra">{{cite news |author1=Jiang Ziwen ({{lang|zh|蒋子文}}) |url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_27201705?commTag=true |script-title=zh:中科院院士、厦门大学教授万惠霖辞世，享年86岁 |work=thepaper |date=28 April 2024 |access-date=30 April 2024 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="rb">{{cite news |url=https://new.qq.com/rain/a/20240428A09IKJ00 |script-title=zh:中国科学院院士、著名物理化学家、教育家万惠霖逝世 |work=qq.com |date=28 April 2024 |access-date=30 April 2024 |language=zh}}</ref> He attended the First Affiliated Middle School of [[Central China Normal University]]. In 1958, he enrolled at the Central South University of Mining and Metallurgy (now [[Central South University]]), where he majored in the Metallurgical Department.<ref name="ra"/><ref name="rb"/> In 1959, due to the adjustment of university and colleges departments, he was transferred to the Department of Chemistry, [[Xiamen University]].<ref name="ra"/><ref name="rb"/>

After graduating in 1962, Wan stayed for teaching.<ref name="ra"/><ref name="rb"/> In 1982, he became a visiting scholar at the Department of Chemistry, [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://alumni.xmu.edu.cn/info/1027/25121.htm |script-title=zh:不懈探索无私奉献——记中科院院士、共产党员万惠霖教授 |work=xmu.edu.cn |date=27 September 2005 |access-date=30 April 2024 |language=zh}}</ref>

On 28 April 2024, he died in [[Xiamen]], [[Fujian]], at the age of 85.<ref name="ra"/><ref name="rb"/>

== Honours and awards ==
* 1986 State Natural Science Award (Third Class) for the research on nitrogen fixation to ammonia under the action of nitrogenase and iron catalyst.
* 1997 Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS)<ref name="ra"/><ref name="rb"/>
* 2001 National Labor Medal<ref name="ra"/><ref name="rb"/>
